items.title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke released on bail; told to sign a one-year peace bond
items.summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, who was placed under preventive arrest by the Delhi Police on October 16, was released on bail today following an order by a special executive magistrate in Delhi, according to LiveLaw . Dipke was detained that evening as he tried to make his way to Connaught Place to participate in the ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ protest called by the CJP at Central Park. The conditions of his bail are not yet clear, but according to LiveLaw , he has been asked to sign a peace bond requiring him to maintain peace and public tranquillity for a year, as stated under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS). Section 126 empowers an executive magistrate to take preventive action against anyone likely to cause a breach of the peace or a public disturbance. According to the police, they initiated action under Sections 126 and 170 (preventive arrest without a warrant or a magistrate’s order) of the BNSS against Dipke. Neha Bora, who was also detained that evening while she was marching from Mandi House, was released earlier today. items.title: Mini Cooper crash: Kerala court denies bail to accused Suhail Sajeev and 3 others
items.summary: A Kerala court on Saturday denied bail to Suhail Sajeev and three others, booked in connection with the Mini Cooper car accident which led to the death of three motorcyclists. Sajeev along with Ninav, Joel and Ameer had filed bail applications before a trial court in Angamaly. However, Judicial First Class Magistrate Samyuktha MK dismissed their bail pleas. The case stemmed from an accident which happened on October 11 when a Mini Cooper driven by Sajeev at high speed hit a scooter carrying three youngsters on the Athani-Airport Road in Nedumbassery, killing all three. According to the First Information Report (FIR), the impact threw all three onto the road, causing severe injuries to their heads and bodies. While two of them died on the spot, the third succumbed to injuries later. The Nedumbassery Airport Police Station registered a case under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The police subsequently arrested Sajeev and three others in connection with the incident. The three were riding in the car along with Sajeev, who was behind the wheel. items.title: PIL in Calcutta High Court seeks double-side printing on A4 paper for pleadings in West Bengal courts
items.summary: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed before the Calcutta High Court seeking a uniform mandate for filing physical pleadings and documents in 75 GSM A4 paper in duplex (back-to-back) format in the High Court and other courts across West Bengal [Akash Sharma v. Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta and Another] . The PIL aims to lower paper consumption, printing services and costs and the physical bulk of court records. The case is listed for hearing on November 23. Calcutta High Court on February 22, 2021 had asked its administrative side to consider mandating use of A4 paper with double-side printing for pleadings and filings. However, the plea filed by advocate Akash Sharma states that further progress of the matter could not be ascertained through publicly available records or notices. This PIL primarily seeks to determine the outcome of the order dated February 22, 2021 and a fresh consideration of the matter to prescribe a uniform practice of using 75 GSM A4 paper in a duplex-printed format across all courts in the State.
